Resolve the selected task with `pose context --task <typed-or-qualified-artifact-ref> --json` before reviewing. Follow its canonical authority and stop on ambiguity, stale binding, unsupported metadata or `transfer-in-progress`. Use the qualified `xref:` scope for cross-project review; every cross-project write requires an explicit `POSE_PROJECT_ROOTS` binding and the current `context_revision` as `--expect-context`. Keep review evidence and its `POSE-Spec:` trailer in the authority repository.

## Steps

1. Classify the change as feature, bugfix, refactor, documentation, or mixed.
2. Run `pose assess tech-debt` during code review to ensure markers (`TODO`, `FIXME`, `stub`, `panic`) are covered by follow-ups or specs. Run `pose assess integrate` when touching inter-module contracts (Protobuf, Kafka, REST, MCP).
3. Resolve `pose review bundle <scope> --explain` to inspect effective criteria, components and tool requirements.
4. Run active required tools first, record why each recommended tool was used or skipped, and keep completion tools deferred until attestation.
5. Select rules with `pose suggest review --path <affected-dir>` for every mapped component.
6. Search `.pose/knowledge/` for prior module decisions, accepted risks, and pending follow-ups.
7. Require deterministic `pose validate --strict` evidence matching delivery targets.
8. Evaluate every required plan criterion, including cross-component boundaries. When the change adds or alters a governance gate, also answer: what is the cheapest way to satisfy this gate in form without producing its value, and what stops that? Point to the adversarial corpus case that proves it (`pose-mcp/internal/cli/testdata/adversarial/README.md`), or record the gap.
9. Classify findings as critical, high, medium, or low with evidence and expected action.
10. Run `pose recurrence-check --tolerant --window-days 14`; use recurrence escalation for a matching systemic signal.
11. Create a handoff with `pose new-knowledge handoff <slug>` for accepted residual risk, monitoring, or deferred action.
12. Seal the review subject with `pose review bundle <scope> --seal`.
13. Prepare the mechanical half with `pose review auto-attest <bundle-id> --reviewer agent:<id>` — without `--apply` — and read `review_attestation.pending`: those are the criteria no registered check answers, and they are yours to answer. Then record the attestation with `pose review attest`, giving every judgment criterion a conclusion. `--apply` on auto-attest records only when nothing is pending; it refuses otherwise, and never answers a judgment criterion for you. An explicit attestation records `--criterion ID|passed|evidence` (or `not-applicable` with a rationale, or `finding` naming a recorded finding) and `--finding ID|severity|disposition|action|evidence[|owner|rationale|review-by]`; every finding needs a severity and an action, and an `accepted-risk` or `wont-fix` finding also needs an owner, a rationale and a review date. A `passed` criterion may cite only evidence the sealed bundle contains, of a class the criterion accepts. For a cross-project attestation, use the qualified `xref:` as the target argument to `pose review attest`, include `--expect-context <digest>` with `--apply`, and keep the explicit project binding; a bundle ID alone does not select an authority project.
14. Run `pose review verify <scope>` and `pose review-check <scope>`; close only when both confirm a valid, approved attestation.
15. Decide: approved, approved with reservations, changes requested, or rejected.
16. When Contributor Mode is active, if review uncovers POSE linter false-positives, diagnostic frictions, or rule gaps, stage an improvement proposal with `pose contribute stage --type enhancement --title "<summary>"`.

## Output requirements

- Completed Rules applied during review section.
- Bundle/plan digests and dispositions for required, recommended and deferred completion tools.
- Severity-classified findings with expected actions.
- Clear and actionable final decision.
- Handoff when residual risk is accepted.

## Quick editorial checklist

- Language is imperative and direct.
- Bullets are short and non-overlapping.
- Files do not duplicate sections.
- `check`, `spec`, and `workflow` are used consistently.
- References point to explicit files or paths.

## Precedence in multi-domain conflicts

- Apply the most restrictive security, contract, and operational rule when domain rules conflict.
- Prefer verifiable check evidence and explicit risk mitigation when speed conflicts with control.
- Record the precedence decision and objective rationale in the review.

## Recurrence traceability

> Also apply: [.pose/rules/_base-recurrence.md](_base-recurrence.md)
# Rule: Knowledge Governance

## When to consult

Consult this guide when creating, updating, reviewing, or removing artifacts under `.pose/knowledge/`.

## TTL and retention

- Set `expires_at` on every artifact when it is created.
- Use a default TTL of 30 days for notes, decision logs, and handoffs.
- Use a TTL of up to 90 days only with a justification recorded in the artifact body.
- Treat an artifact without `expires_at` as non-compliant and block its creation or merge.

## When this is not the right home

- Use `.pose/knowledge/` only for time-bound operational memory: content
  tied to a decision moment, a handoff between executions, or something
  meant to be reviewed and eventually expire.
- A durable fact or convention that will not become false and carries no
  review trigger — a third-party tool's parsing quirk, a naming
  convention, a recurring gotcha — is not a `decision-log` just because no
  better type exists. Route it to `.pose/rules/` instead: add it to an
  existing rule file or create one, then wire it into the relevant task
  type's base `rules` array in `.pose/indexes/task-map.json` so
  `pose suggest <task>` surfaces it automatically. No path scoping is
  required — a task type's base `rules` list is returned regardless of
  `--path`; only language/component-specific rules need the
  `rules_by_domain` layer.
- Rule of thumb: if nothing was decided or traded off, and nothing about
  the fact will change on a predictable timeline, it is not a
  `decision-log` and not an ADR — it is a rule. See ADR
  `2026-08-15-durable-non-architectural-knowledge-belongs-in-rules-not-a-new-type`.

## Reusable cross-execution format

- Structure reusable context as a handoff with fixed sections: Context, Current state, Next checks, Risks, and Next owner.
- Keep `source_refs` linked to the relevant spec, workflow, and executed check commands.
- Record `last_reviewed_at` in the body to make effective cross-execution updates traceable.

## Archiving and purging

- Run biweekly triage to list expired artifacts.
- Move expired artifacts to `.pose/knowledge/archive/` when they retain audit value.
- Purge archived artifacts 180 days after expiration unless documented legal or compliance requirements apply.
- Record every archive and purge action in the housekeeping log.

## Sensitive content

- Prohibit secrets, tokens, credentials, private keys, and equivalent material.
- Prohibit personal data and non-anonymized customer data.
- Do not copy restricted incidents or reports in full; keep only a controlled reference.
- Classify frontmatter `sensitivity` as `public-internal` or `restricted`.
- Remove identified sensitive content immediately and open a security follow-up.

## Ownership and review

- Keep `@pose-maintainers` as the primary governance owner.
- Require an owner in every artifact frontmatter.
- Review expiration biweekly and quality monthly.
- Escalate a backlog overdue by more than two cycles to the primary owner.
- Block backlog growth when `list-expired` exceeds the operational limit: zero in strict mode, two in tolerant mode.

## Minimum operational checks

- Run `pose knowledge-check --strict` biweekly to validate the expired backlog.
- Run `pose knowledge-housekeeping list-expired` for detailed triage.
- Run `pose knowledge-housekeeping archive-expired --dry-run` before applying changes.
- Execute destructive actions only with an explicit `--apply` flag.

.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:113:## 7. Final Report
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:115:### Delivered scope
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:116:One bounded cache (bytes, global and per worktree, least recently used, optional expiry) carries the parsed delivery graph, the design-delta report and the test catalog; the paths of a commit are read by the governed capture, bounded in output (4 MiB) and in paths (100,000) and not cached, because every governed read is audited. A missed key is produced once however many callers ask, after reserving the bytes it expects to hold against global and per-worktree in-flight budgets, with a cap on productions and on waiters per key; a waiter that leaves does not disturb the producer or the others; a failure is never remembered; a value over its budget, or declared unretainable, is served and neither retained nor copied for retention; copies run outside the lock. Parsed graphs are keyed by engine, schema and the digest of the bytes, so identical bytes share an entry and nothing is served another worktree's graph. The test catalog is keyed by root and the digest of the validation matrix and expires after 30 seconds. The deep isolation is structural: a reflection test fills every slice, map and pointer of the graph and finds the references a copy shares with the original, which reproduced the aliasing the audit had not reproduced (the node attribute maps and the roadmap criteria refs) and fixed it. Read-only consumers can view the graph without a copy (`ViewDeliveryIntegrity`). Left out: moving every consumer to the view, RSS measurement, any persistent or cross-process cache, any global Git pool.

.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:126:### Residual risks
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:127:- The clone a caller keeps is the caller's memory and is outside the budget; the view exists for readers that keep nothing. So are the inputs a caller read before asking the cache (the raw index bytes a waiter holds) and the clone being made for a caller: the cache charges what it keeps alive for itself, retained entries, productions, shared results until their last waiter copied them, and pinned entries. Bounding what callers allocate before and after the call is not done here; reading a smaller input is the follow-up below.
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:128:- An overloaded catalog cache is reported: lint-spec and the closeout gate fail with "test references could not be verified" instead of treating the missing catalog as an empty one; callers that only skip resolution keep the lenient form.
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:130:- The estimate of retained bytes errs high, so the cache holds less than its budget in practice.
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:133:### Follow-ups
.pose/specs/2026-10-14-pose-bounded-isolated-graph-caches.md:137:- [open] Bound what callers hold around the cache: read the delivery index in a bounded stream or by a size-gated admission before the bytes are allocated, and reserve the bytes of the clone a caller is about to receive.
